## Owner and exhaustive consumption boundary

The chosen class is under-specified observations of an individual channel
intent's state/disposition. The parent is fixture-authority and observation
identity drift under #2151/#2542. The local failing query was an entry point,
not the boundary. All34 original waiter calls, the waiter/carrier construction
and restart chain, and all eight known sibling clusters migrate together.

Existing backend channeldelivery.ObserveIntent owns kind + provider +
provider_event_id + interface_key, including exact uniqueness refusal.
runtimepersistence validates the selected owner and enters its read boundary;
storetest.ChannelObservation is the existing process read-only inspection
adapter. No new SQL port, table dispatcher, predicate fallback, transaction
protocol or capability owner. The served waiter and single-attempt helper only
consume channeldelivery.Observer; source-aware ingress capture is fixture-local.

All34 calls now supply the actual narrow observer and captured tuple. Typed
capture happens after actual onboarding readiness, before ingress/rebind cuts.
Retained occurrences keep predecessor identity; new ingress after rebind uses
the newly admitted tuple. Source restart with no live activation uses the
existing channel.list recovery provider, which the onboarding owner resolves
against the exact interface in the current compiled catalog. This is identity
metadata, not a fixed-history certificate or recreated execution authority.
Missing/contradictory identity fails immediately. Observer cleanup is registered
at opening, and stop/kill/restart boundaries close and reopen it explicitly.

Sibling consumption is exhaustive within the amended class:
- Receptionist rejection: original polling, actual action tuple, no SQL opener.
- Uncertain-copy rebind: actual901110 ingress identity, old-destination refusal
  and provider-output conservation retained.
- Stale controls: update and update+1 are independent canonical observations;
  optional cancel update+3 shares their original deadline. Text update+2 keeps
  its separate original deadline. Duplicate requests/status assertions remain.
- Draft teaching/rejection: exact text/action tuple, original15s/20ms polling
  and allowed terminal alternatives, with explicit observer restart boundaries.
- Token-substring callback helper: deleted across all five callers; each uses
  its actual posted occurrence, never a reused token as occurrence identity.
- ACK process-death: the same exact query at immediate found pending/empty
  disposition while the provider barrier is held and at recovered settled/
  applied. ACK attempt/count, business count, kill and restart remain unchanged.
- Selected-fork source: exact child unsupported occurrence, original5s/20ms
  gate, upstream refusal, parent/child conservation, duplicate/restart and
  ordinary-run assertions retained. The posting bridge returns HTTP status
  separately from a query derived from the exact posted update_id payload.

Repository sibling scan finds only the retained global intent counts, complete
history witnesses and provenance response projection outside this class.
waitNativeIntentCount and populated/global-zero/history snapshots need total
or physical-row evidence, not one exact occurrence; they remain parent debt.
waitObjectIntentResponse proves publication/plan/receipt provenance and still
has an event-ID-only predicate: this is an explicitly open projection/identity
risk in #2542, not an already-safe sibling. The physical-fact owner remains
separate too. providerAliasActionIntentStorage consumes the exact publication
receipt's physical fact rather than substituting token/occurrence settlement.
No channel-wide identity closure claim is made.
